description: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output across different layers of a large language model, using a threshold of 1e-3 to define sparsity. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 22, with tick marks at intervals of 5, representing the depth of the model’s transformer layers. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.8, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2, indicating the proportion of attention weights below the threshold. Three distinct lines are plotted: a blue dashed line representing the sparsity ratio before gating, which remains near zero across all layers (average 0.003); an orange dotted line for the sparsity ratio after gating, which starts near 0.8 at layer 0, drops sharply to below 0.2 by layer 5, and then fluctuates slightly around 0.02–0.08 for later layers (average 0.126); and a green dash-dotted line for the sparsity ratio after average gating, which begins near 0.8, declines steeply to below 0.1 by layer 5, and stabilizes near 0.02–0.04 for layers beyond 10 (average 0.080). All three lines show a general trend of decreasing sparsity with increasing layer depth, with the gated variants exhibiting significantly higher sparsity than the pre-gate baseline.
